# PARONYCHIA

Cutaneous infection of the hand, cuticle or fingers usually occurring near OR around the nail. Treatment depends on etiology. Candida spp. are commonly involved when the patient has extensive exposure to water (e.g. dishwashers). Staphylococcus aureus is more commonly after manicures or nail biting. Herpes simplex (whitlow) usually follows exposure to oral mucosa (e.g. wrestlers, dentists, or anesthetists).

## Treatment for paronychia associated with Candida

Preferred:
Treat for 14 days
Clotrimazole 1% apply to affected area once daily ($) [M]

Alternative:
Nystatin Cream to affected area BID ($) [M]

## Treatment for paronychia associated with Staphylococcus

Preferred:
Treat for 10 days
Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO BID ($) [R,DI]

Alternative:
Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID ($) [DI]
